response.sql: WITH channel_rates AS (SELECT o.orderbase, AVG(f.feerate) AS average_fee_rate FROM fees AS f JOIN orders AS o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault WHERE f.feerate IS NOT NULL AND o.orderbase IS NOT NULL GROUP BY o.orderbase), overall AS (SELECT AVG(f.feerate) AS average_fee_rate FROM fees AS f JOIN orders AS o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault WHERE f.feerate IS NOT NULL AND o.orderbase IS NOT NULL) SELECT AVG(c.average_fee_rate) AS mean_average_fee_rate, AVG(c.average_fee_rate - a.average_fee_rate) AS mean_amount_above_average FROM channel_rates AS c CROSS JOIN overall AS a WHERE c.average_fee_rate > a.average_fee_rate

assumptions.assumption: The benchmark is the average across linked fee records with a known order channel, so channels with more fees have more weight in the benchmark.

alternatives.interpretation: Give each channel equal weight when calculating the benchmark average.
